primary_claim: On the BIG-bench Simple Ethical Questions benchmark, state-of-the-art LLMs identify morally objectionable actions with high accuracy overall, but some heavily fine-tuned/aligned models (notably larger Claude models) perform worse than smaller models and jailbroken variants because they refuse to answer more often.

effect.metric: accuracy on BIG-bench Simple Ethical Questions
effect.value: GPT-4 and Llama-3.3-70B-instruct: 0.992; DeepSeek R1/V3: 0.969; Claude 3.5 Haiku: 0.962; Claude accuracy decreases as model size increases; jailbroken Llama-3.1-8B-instruct rises from 50.77% to 90.00%

stated_future_work: Investigate why this behaviour occurs, by comparing AI labs' official safety policies
Compare Claude's and Llama's refusals across non-ethical tasks to determine if it can be observed more generally
Consider AI alignment methods to enable appropriate engagement with sensitive material
limitations_stated: Parameter counts for closed-source models are speculative
Could not replicate earlier published BIG-bench results using an older version of the task
quote: However, some heavily fine-tuned models perform worse on this task than smaller models and jailbroken variants. These results suggest that fine-tuning methods can correlate with increased reluctance to engage with ethical questions, potentially at the cost of moral judgment.
